map.输入胜率、盈亏比或单笔可承受亏损资金，用凯利公式 f* = W − (1−W)/: Enter the win rate, the payoff ratio or the tolerable per-trade loss capital and use the Kelly formula f* = W - (1-W)/R to get the optimal position fraction, or determine the order size by the fixed-risk method.
map.固定风险：股数 = 资金 × 风险% / |入场价 − 止损价|；凯利：f* =: Fixed risk: shares = capital x risk % / |entry - stop|; Kelly: f* = win rate - loss rate / payoff ratio (half Kelly = f* / 2)
map.固定分数法先确定单笔可承受亏损（资金×风险%），再除以每股风险得到仓位；凯利公式: The fixed-fraction method first sets the tolerable loss per trade (capital x risk %), then divides by the per-share risk to get the position; the Kelly formula gives the optimal bet fraction from the win rate and payoff ratio, and half Kelly is common in practice to reduce drawdown.
map.按可承受风险金额与每股风险，算应买股数（固定风险法）。: From the tolerable risk amount and the per-share risk, compute the shares to buy (fixed-risk method).
map.凯利公式估算最优下注比例（f=(W−L)/W，W 胜率、L 赔率相关）。: The Kelly formula estimates the optimal bet fraction (f = (W - L)/W, where W is the win rate and L relates to the odds).
map.账户 10 万、单笔风险 2%、每股风险 2 元: Account of 100,000 CNY, single-trade risk 2%, per-share risk 2 CNY
map.：可承受损失=10 万×2%=2000 元；股数=2000/2=1000 股。即: Tolerable loss = 100,000 x 2% = 2000 CNY; shares = 2000/2 = 1000 shares. That is, at most 1000 shares, losing 2000 CNY at a 2 CNY per-share stop.
map.：胜率 55%、赔率 1（盈亏比 1:1）：f=(0.55×1−0.45)/1=: With a 55% win rate and odds of 1 (a 1:1 payoff): f = (0.55 x 1 - 0.45)/1 = 0.10, so full Kelly is 10% and half Kelly 5%. Half Kelly is more robust and lowers ruin risk.

map.固定风险法和凯利冲突？: Do the Fixed-Risk and Kelly Methods Conflict?
map.不冲突：凯利定\"账户比例\"，固定风险法定\"每股止损对应的股数\"。实务常取: No conflict: Kelly sets the "account fraction", while the fixed-risk method sets "shares per unit of stop loss". In practice, half Kelly combined with a fixed-risk constraint is common.
map.凯利公式的前提？: What Are the Preconditions of the Kelly Formula?
map.假设独立重复赌博、概率与赔率已知且稳定。实盘概率估计有误差，故用半凯利或更保守比: It assumes independent repeated gambles with known and stable probabilities and odds. Real probabilities carry estimation error, so use half Kelly or a more conservative fraction.
